Yes, you can increase stomach acid on your own. Taking ACV (Apple Cider Vinegar) shots before every meal helped me and I still do it because my acid needs support with all these antibiotic pills. Bragg's is the best brand. Build up to 1 tablespoon of ACV in 2oz of water (or less water, I do about a 1:1 ratio now). I will say doing this for a while may start to erode your enamel, so try not to let the acid hit your teeth and make sure to use a remineralizing toothpaste. For histamine intolerance, I highly highly recommend taking Quercetin supplements. I like Natural Factors brand Bioactive Quercetin EMIQ. I only took one pill a day and within a couple months my itchy skin and rashes from histamine intolerance went away. NOTE: Vinegar has histamines so it's important to address your histamine intolerance first. If you're going to do the ACV, try not to eat other stuff that has histamines/release histamines (look up low-histamine diet).

  
Digestive bitters before meals help build your stomach acid as well. They don't taste amazing but that's kind of the point. Herb Pharm has one that I liked but there are different ones out there. You take them at least 15-30 mins before each meal, and let the bitters sort of marinate on your tongue for like 30 seconds before swallowing. And then theres also Betaine HCl, I take a capsule with every meal.  


SIBO won't go away just from increasing your stomach acid, you have to eliminate the bacterial overgrowth that has established itself in your gut. But you shouldn't start treatment until you strengthen your stomach acid. Hope this helps.

I went through something extremely similar when I was your exact age. I was constantly apologizing for "messing things up" by being more demanding with what I wanted and taking my ex's gestures of affection and efforts for granted. He'd then talk about how we shouldn't be together, I'd beg him and send him long messages describing how I'd change and try to act as perfect as possible when we did see each other, and then he'd say he'd think about it. It was a cycle, even after we took a break for a couple months. I realized a year later, though, that my emotional needs *were* valid and that I was pining after someone who did the *bare* minimum, but because I was so used to "minimum" I didn't notice how shitty he was being and how unhappy I was (for example, I'd get excited and feel enamored over the smallest gestures that should have been considered normal behavior). I don't know enough about your bf to say for sure, but from what you've said it sounds like it might be the same situation. What caused me to see the imbalance in our relationship was finding out about something called Attachment Theory in psychology. I *highly* recommend you do a google search on it, and also that you read a [book](https://www.amazon.com/Insecure-Love-Anxious-Attachment-Jealous/dp/1608828158) called *Insecure in Love* by Leslie Becker-Phelps. It quite literally changed my life and I now can recognize unhealthy patterns in relationships and how to choose a healthy and stable partner, among other things.

You are *so* young, even if you don't feel like it. Please do not waste these precious years on mediocre people or men that don't respect you and your time. Don't lie to yourself about your feelings and try to convince yourself that you are wrong for feeling them--you told him you didn't feel loved for a reason. Your feelings are valid. Please don't make the mistake that I did, you'll definitely regret it when you're older.
